comment: The harness's own dated deferrals, as reviewed data — the ONE machine-read home for every dated deferral sentence in the harness-OWNED prose surfaces (docs/harness/gates-catalog.md, the top-level tools/*.mjs gate scripts, tools/auth-posture.json). tools/check-docs-sync.mjs closes sentence <-> entry BOTH ways and reds an entry whose target this install has reached: at the named release the author must ship the deferred check or move the date in a reviewed diff. This file is harness-owned and git-clean-enforced by check-gate-integrity's tools/ surface, so moving a date is a deliberate act that appears in the PR diff — a date can never roll silently again, which is what happened before this ledger existed: three prose sites carried the same stale promise into the release it named, with nothing reading any of them. `file` is one path or an ARRAY of paths when a single decision is stated at several sites; every listed file must carry the dated sentence, at this entry's exact target. enforcement-tiers.md is deliberately NOT ledgered here — its Target column has its own reader in check-docs-sync.mjs (the surface derivation and the closes: probe) — and SEEDED files are the consumer's prose, not the harness's to red (tools/data-flow.json's export target has its own enforcement in check-data-flow.mjs).

deferrals.reason: The standing ask-the-CLI section census (reading the Supabase CLI's own deprecation warnings instead of a hand-maintained knownSections list). The 0.6.0 spike built it, it worked, and it found the shipped [inbucket] rename — but the blocker is UPSTREAM, not scheduling. RE-CHECKED AT 0.9.0 (2026-08-10): npm latest is still 2.113.0 — the exact version the 0.8.0 re-check read — the newest artifacts are v2.114.0 betas whose only config-adjacent change is a docker postgrest image bump, the Go CLI's `config` command group still registers exactly one subcommand, `push` (no --dry-run; needs a project ref and the management API), and the exact ask is still open upstream as https://github.com/supabase/cli/issues/5894 ('Add a `supabase config validate` preflight command', no milestone, no linked PR). The original spike findings stand: `functions list` needs an access token, and `status` — the one that runs — binds to whatever stack holds the default ports (it reported another project's containers) and prints SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET into output a gate would then handle. A safe standing check needs a side-effect-free `config lint`-shaped subcommand; re-check for one at every CLI pin bump. THE STANDING RULE (the 0.8.0 move licensed itself 'once'; the 0.9.0 arrival proved the shape recurs, so the rule is now written): each time the target arrives with the upstream condition still unmet, the arrival forces the re-check and the date moves ONE minor in a reviewed diff across every listed site — the scanner's red firing on schedule IS the mechanism, and a discharge happens only when the upstream subcommand actually ships.
